'''Eugene Huu-Chau "Gene" Trinh''' ([[Vietnamese language|Vietnamese]]: Trịnh Hữu Châu, born September 14, 1950) is a [[Vietnamese American]] biochemist who flew aboard NASA Space Shuttle mission [[STS-50]]<ref>{{Cite web|title = Spaceflight mission report: STS-50|url = http://www.spacefacts.de/mission/english/sts-50.htm|website = www.spacefacts.de|accessdate = 2015-09-23|first = Joachim|last = Becker}}</ref> as a [[Payload Specialist]], becoming the first Vietnamese American astronaut in space<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sandiegoairandspace.org/exhibits/asian_american_exhibit/ |title=Asian-Americans in Aviation Online Exhibition |work=Exhibits |publisher=San Diego Air & Space Museum |accessdate=20 November 2012 |quote=Dr. Trinh is the first Vietnamese-American to go to outer space. }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title = Vietnamese Americans|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=MUQBHyZOvwcC|publisher = [[Infobase Publishing]]|date = 2007-01-01|isbn = 9781438107172|first = Liz|last = Sonneborn}}</ref> and the second Vietnamese in space (after cosmonaut [[Phạm Tuân]]).

==Biography==
Trinh was born in [[Saigon]], [[South Vietnam]]. Trinh moved with his parents to [[Paris]], France, when he was two years old. He came to the United States to study when he was 18 and later became an American citizen.<ref name="bionasa">{{cite web|url=https://www.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/atoms/files/trinh.pdf |title=Eugene H. Trinh (Ph.D.), Payload Specialist |date=April 1996 |access-date=March 31, 2023|publisher=NASA}}</ref>

Trinh graduated from Lycee Michelet in Paris, France, in 1968 with a baccalaureate degree. He received a Bachelor of Science degree in Mechanical Engineering-Applied Physics from [[Columbia University]] in 1972.<ref>{{Cite web|title=12 Groundbreaking Asian Columbians You Should Know|url=https://news.columbia.edu/news/12-groundbreaking-asian-columbians-you-should-know|access-date=2022-02-11|website=Columbia News|language=en}}</ref> He then studied at [[Yale University]], earning a Masters of Science in 1974, a Masters of Philosophy in 1975, and a Doctorate of Philosophy in Applied Physics in 1977.<ref name="yale">{{Cite web|title=Yale Bulletin and Calendar - NASA needs more engineers, says alumnus astronaut|url=http://archives.news.yale.edu/v31.n26/story4.html|access-date=2022-02-11|website=archives.news.yale.edu}}</ref>

==Career==
Trinh served as the director of the physical sciences research division in the Biological and Physical Research Enterprise at [[NASA]] headquarters.<ref name="yale"/> He started with  NASA in 1979, as a senior research scientist at the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]]. He conducted experimental and theoretical research in fluid dynamics, fundamental materials science, and levitation technology for 20 years. He performed hands-on experimental investigations in laboratories aboard the NASA KC-135 aircraft, and on the [[Space Shuttle Columbia|Space Shuttle ''Columbia'']].<ref name="bionasa"/>

Trinh was a payload specialist crew member on the STS-50/United States Microgravity Lab-1 Space Shuttle flight in 1992.<ref name="bionasa"/>

As director of the physical sciences research division at NASA, Trinh leads the effort to develop an innovative peer-reviewed scientific program focusing on the effects of gravity on physical, chemical, and biological systems. The results of this program will enable the human exploration and development of space, providing the scientific basis for technologies permitting humankind to explore the vast expanses of the [[Solar System]] and beyond.<ref name="yale"/>

In May 2004, Trinh received the Golden Torch Award from the Vietnamese American National Gala in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref>{{cite web|title=The Famous "Who's Who" You Probably Didn't Know|date=September 5, 2010|author=Sarah Bui |url=https://talk.onevietnam.org/the-famous-whos-who-you-probably-didnt-know/|website=onevietnam.org|access-date=March 31, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Stepp |first=Laura Sessions |date=2004-05-11 |title=A Generation Takes Root on New Soil |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/2004/05/11/a-generation-takes-root-on-new-soil/46a25c2c-2453-4793-96ba-cfc0994ebc95/ |access-date=2026-02-13 |work=[[The Washington Post]] |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

Trinh formerly resided in [[Culver City, California]], but now makes his home in [[McLean, Virginia]]. He is married to the former Yvette Fabry and has one child.
